c139d4c9f579e462e1c170864fbc73edea1b2b82: El Tarter's 215 km of runs make for a fine offer for all profiles: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 74 lifts let you link descents without long queues. El Tarter's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Pyrenees for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2640 m and a village at 1710 m, El Tarter's snow reliability is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause strains early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. A stay in El Tarter is clearly on the expensive side: €69 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but it is worth being aware of it before you set off. In short: El Tarter lives up to its promises. A Pyrenees resort that will suit the majority of profiles without disappointing.

c1abb96f5575b97216fa78de2e94c7d56df8b413: Carì is a small, low-key resort: 20 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues whatsoever at the lifts. Carì's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Carì's altitude (1650 m at the bottom, 2280 m at the top) helps it keep decent snow cover through midwinter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it's best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Carì is clearly high: 51€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you set off. In short: Carì doesn't rival the ski giants, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.
